verdict.rationale: Pipedream's docs say Connect provides built-in user authentication, so developers do not build authorization flows or handle token storage and refresh, and that this is handled automatically by the MCP server. Credentials are encrypted at rest and proxied through Pipedream's servers, never exposed to models. Missing for 10: OAuth is not explicitly named (only 'authorization flows'), token refresh is covered by a single brief sentence with no mechanics, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can let the platform run OAuth flows for downstream tools and vault the resulting credentials encrypted, with automatic token refresh

citations.quote: Pipedream Connect includes built-in user authentication for more than APIs via MCP, which means you don’t need to build any authorization flows or deal with token storage and refresh
This is handled automatically by Pipedream’s MCP server and there’s no additional implementation required
User credentials are encrypted at rest and all requests are made through Pipedream's servers, never directly exposing credentials to AI models.
the proxy forwards your request with the connected user's credentials attached
